result.title: PACT: Plan-Action Consistency Training by Preserving Correct Plans and Repairing Actions in GUI Agents
result.summary: GUI agents can formulate a correct immediate plan in their reasoning yet emit an action that fails to execute it, creating an execution gap. This recurring mismatch undermines reliable task completion, as a single execution error can derail a multi-step workflow. In outcome-supervised reinforcement learning, broadcasting a negative response-level advantage across all generated tokens risks penalizing valid planning together with erroneous execution. To address this credit-assignment conflict, we introduce PACT (Plan-Action Consistency Training), a training framework that combines reference-aligned plan protection and plan-aligned action repair without altering the original scalar action reward. Using annotated reference actions to identify execution gaps, PACT protects the verified plan by masking negative policy-gradient contributions across its token span. Keeping the generated reasoning unchanged as context, it then favors the reference action over the emitted erroneous action through a preference surrogate with stop-gradient pair weights. Compared with the outcome-only baseline, PACT raises AndroidWorld task success from 60.34% to 68.97% (+8.63 pp), while improving rule-based plan-action consistency on AndroidControl High from 83.71% to 89.74% (+6.03 pp). Adapting PACT to desktop agents also improves task success from 40.92% to 44.17% (+3.25 pp) on the full 369-task OSWorld benchmark. Together, these results establish PACT as an effective credit-assignment framework for bridging execution gaps and improving task completion across mobile and desktop GUI environments.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对 GUI agent 中「计划正确但动作执行错误」的执行鸿沟，提出 PACT 训练框架：用参考动作定位执行失败，遮蔽推理计划片段上的负向策略梯度以保护已验证计划，再用偏好替代目标修复动作，在 AndroidWorld、AndroidControl 与 OSWorld 上取得提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 关注的贡献分配与监督直接相关：把结果级 advantage 拆分到推理计划与动作 token 上，可供核查其思路是否适用于 latent 推理状态的信用分配，以及「答案是否真正使用推理内容」的诊断。
